What comes up in Camden

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Rural outbuildings and farm structures

Steel and timber framed sheds with cement sheet roofing, concrete pads and old fencing.

How it is handled
Sheeting assessed and removed under licence where it is asbestos, then the frames down and the pads broken out.
What does it
Midi to large excavator with a grapple and a hammer, truck and dogs for the volume.

Older village dwelling

Pre-war and inter-war stock on smaller blocks close to the centre, frequently with neighbours close on both sides.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, then careful demolition with the neighbouring structures protected and the work kept inside the approved hours.
What does it
Smaller machines and hand work at the boundaries.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Camden

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Village stock and rural blocks side by side Camden has buildings going back generations a short distance from new estate housing, and they are not the same job.
  • Heritage controls in the older parts Which settle what can be removed before a demolition scope is written, and are worth resolving early.
  • Rural outbuildings Sheds, stables and farm structures where weathered fibro is common.
  • Room to work on most blocks Which usually means material can be separated on site rather than carted mixed.

Camden ranges from tight older village streets to open rural frontages, and the access varies with it. On the rural blocks a truck and dog is usually viable; in the older centre the question is whether anything can stand at the kerb at all.

Camden questions

What people ask before we start

The building is old. Does that stop us demolishing it?
Not necessarily, but it is a planning question before it is a demolition one. Whether a structure is listed or sits in a conservation area determines what can be removed, and that has to be settled with the consent authority rather than assumed.
Do you work on rural properties?
Yes. Sheds, stables, silos and farm structures are a regular part of the work out here, and there is usually room to do it properly.
Why does the haul distance matter out here?
Because the destination is set by what the material is classified as rather than by what is closest, and from the south west the licensed facility for a given classification can be a long way off. It is a real line in the price rather than a rounding error.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
